#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal ISO9660 reader: parse PVD, walk directory tree, extract files by name."""
import sys, struct

ISO = "/app/alpine.iso"
SECTOR = 2048
OUTDIR = "/tmp/isoout"

f = open(ISO, "rb")

def read_sector(lba):
    f.seek(lba * SECTOR)
    return f.read(SECTOR)

# Find Primary Volume Descriptor (sector 16)
pvd = read_sector(16)
assert pvd[1:6] == b"CD001", "not ISO9660?"
assert pvd[0] == 1, "PVD type mismatch"
# Root directory record at offset 156 (34 bytes)
root_dr = pvd[156:156+34]
root_extent = struct.unpack("<I", root_dr[2:6])[0]
root_size = struct.unpack("<I", root_dr[10:14])[0]
print(f"Root extent LBA={root_extent} size={root_size}")

def parse_dir(extent, size):
    """Yield (name, extent_lba, data_len, flags) for records in a directory."""
    f.seek(extent * SECTOR)
    data = f.read(size)
    pos = 0
    while pos < len(data):
        rlen = data[pos]
        if rlen == 0:
            # padding to next sector boundary
            pos = (pos // SECTOR + 1) * SECTOR
            continue
        rec = data[pos:pos+rlen]
        ext = struct.unpack("<I", rec[2:6])[0]
        dlen = struct.unpack("<I", rec[10:14])[0]
        flags = rec[25]
        name_len = rec[32]
        name = rec[33:33+name_len]
        pos += rlen
        if name in (b"\x00", b"\x01"):  # . and ..
            continue
        yield name, ext, dlen, flags

def walk(extent, size, path="/"):
    for name, ext, dlen, flags in parse_dir(extent, size):
        # strip version suffix ';1'
        nm = name.split(b";")[0]
        isdir = bool(flags & 0x02)
        full = path + nm.decode("latin1")
        print(f"{'[DIR] ' if isdir else '      '}{full}  LBA={ext} size={dlen}")
        if isdir:
            walk(ext, dlen, full + "/")

print("=== directory tree ===")
walk(root_extent, root_size)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract specific files from the ISO by directory name match."""
import struct, os

ISO = "/app/alpine.iso"
SECTOR = 2048
f = open(ISO, "rb")

def read_sector(lba):
    f.seek(lba * SECTOR); return f.read(SECTOR)

pvd = read_sector(16)
root_dr = pvd[156:156+34]
root_extent = struct.unpack("<I", root_dr[2:6])[0]
root_size = struct.unpack("<I", root_dr[10:14])[0]

def parse_dir(extent, size):
    f.seek(extent * SECTOR); data = f.read(size); pos = 0
    while pos < len(data):
        rlen = data[pos]
        if rlen == 0:
            pos = (pos // SECTOR + 1) * SECTOR; continue
        rec = data[pos:pos+rlen]
        ext = struct.unpack("<I", rec[2:6])[0]
        dlen = struct.unpack("<I", rec[10:14])[0]
        flags = rec[25]; name_len = rec[32]; name = rec[33:33+name_len]
        pos += rlen
        if name in (b"\x00", b"\x01"): continue
        yield name, ext, dlen, flags

def find(extent, size, target_upper):
    for name, ext, dlen, flags in parse_dir(extent, size):
        nm = name.split(b";")[0]
        if flags & 0x02:
            r = find(ext, dlen, target_upper)
            if r: return r
        if nm.upper() == target_upper:
            return (ext, dlen)
    return None

def extract(target, outpath):
    r = find(root_extent, root_size, target.upper())
    if not r:
        print("NOT FOUND:", target); return
    ext, dlen = r
    f.seek(ext * SECTOR)
    remaining = dlen
    with open(outpath, "wb") as o:
        while remaining > 0:
            chunk = f.read(min(SECTOR*64, remaining))
            if not chunk: break
            o.write(chunk); remaining -= len(chunk)
    print(f"extracted {target} -> {outpath} ({dlen} bytes)")

os.makedirs("/tmp/isoout", exist_ok=True)
extract("boot/vmlinuz-lts", "/tmp/isoout/vmlinuz-lts")
extract("boot/initramfs-lts", "/tmp/isoout/initramfs-lts")
# small text files for reference
extract("boot/syslinux/syslinux.cfg", "/tmp/isoout/syslinux.cfg")
extract(".alpine_release", "/tmp/isoout/alpine_release")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract specific files from the ISO by directory name match."""
import struct, os

ISO = "/app/alpine.iso"
SECTOR = 2048
f = open(ISO, "rb")

def read_sector(lba):
    f.seek(lba * SECTOR); return f.read(SECTOR)

pvd = read_sector(16)
root_dr = pvd[156:156+34]
root_extent = struct.unpack("<I", root_dr[2:6])[0]
root_size = struct.unpack("<I", root_dr[10:14])[0]

def parse_dir(extent, size):
    f.seek(extent * SECTOR); data = f.read(size); pos = 0
    while pos < len(data):
        rlen = data[pos]
        if rlen == 0:
            pos = (pos // SECTOR + 1) * SECTOR; continue
        rec = data[pos:pos+rlen]
        ext = struct.unpack("<I", rec[2:6])[0]
        dlen = struct.unpack("<I", rec[10:14])[0]
        flags = rec[25]; name_len = rec[32]; name = rec[33:33+name_len]
        pos += rlen
        if name in (b"\x00", b"\x01"): continue
        yield name, ext, dlen, flags

def norm(raw):
    # strip version ';1', strip trailing '.', turn '_' into '-' (ISO9660 -> real name)
    s = raw.split(b";")[0].rstrip(b".").replace(b"_", b"-")
    return s.decode("latin1").upper()

def find(extent, size, components):
    """components: list of path parts already normalized UPPER ('BOOT','VMLINUZ-LTS')."""
    head = components[0]
    for name, ext, dlen, flags in parse_dir(extent, size):
        nm = norm(name)
        if flags & 0x02 and nm == head and len(components) > 1:
            r = find(ext, dlen, components[1:])
            if r: return r
        if nm == head and not (flags & 0x02):
            return (ext, dlen)
    return None

def extract(target, outpath):
    comps = [c.upper().replace("_", "-") for c in target.strip("/").split("/") if c]
    r = find(root_extent, root_size, comps)

def extract(target, outpath):
    r = find(root_extent, root_size, target.upper())
    if not r:
        print("NOT FOUND:", target); return
    ext, dlen = r
    f.seek(ext * SECTOR)
    remaining = dlen
    with open(outpath, "wb") as o:
        while remaining > 0:
            chunk = f.read(min(SECTOR*64, remaining))
            if not chunk: break
            o.write(chunk); remaining -= len(chunk)
    print(f"extracted {target} -> {outpath} ({dlen} bytes)")

os.makedirs("/tmp/isoout", exist_ok=True)
extract("boot/vmlinuz-lts", "/tmp/isoout/vmlinuz-lts")
extract("boot/initramfs-lts", "/tmp/isoout/initramfs-lts")
# small text files for reference
extract("boot/syslinux/syslinux.cfg", "/tmp/isoout/syslinux.cfg")
extract(".alpine_release", "/tmp/isoout/alpine_release")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract specific files from the ISO by directory name match."""
import struct, os

ISO = "/app/alpine.iso"
SECTOR = 2048
f = open(ISO, "rb")

def read_sector(lba):
    f.seek(lba * SECTOR); return f.read(SECTOR)

pvd = read_sector(16)
root_dr = pvd[156:156+34]
root_extent = struct.unpack("<I", root_dr[2:6])[0]
root_size = struct.unpack("<I", root_dr[10:14])[0]

def parse_dir(extent, size):
    f.seek(extent * SECTOR); data = f.read(size); pos = 0
    while pos < len(data):
        rlen = data[pos]
        if rlen == 0:
            pos = (pos // SECTOR + 1) * SECTOR; continue
        rec = data[pos:pos+rlen]
        ext = struct.unpack("<I", rec[2:6])[0]
        dlen = struct.unpack("<I", rec[10:14])[0]
        flags = rec[25]; name_len = rec[32]; name = rec[33:33+name_len]
        pos += rlen
        if name in (b"\x00", b"\x01"): continue
        yield name, ext, dlen, flags

def norm(raw):
    # strip version ';1', strip trailing '.', turn '_' into '-' (ISO9660 -> real name)
    s = raw.split(b";")[0].rstrip(b".").replace(b"_", b"-")
    return s.decode("latin1").upper()

def find(extent, size, components):
    """components: list of path parts already normalized UPPER ('BOOT','VMLINUZ-LTS')."""
    head = components[0]
    for name, ext, dlen, flags in parse_dir(extent, size):
        nm = norm(name)
        if flags & 0x02 and nm == head and len(components) > 1:
            r = find(ext, dlen, components[1:])
            if r: return r
        if nm == head and not (flags & 0x02):
            return (ext, dlen)
    return None

def extract(target, outpath):
    comps = [c.upper().replace("_", "-") for c in target.strip("/").split("/") if c]
    r = find(root_extent, root_size, comps)

def extract(target, outpath):
    r = find(root_extent, root_size, target.upper())
    if not r:
        print("NOT FOUND:", target); return
    ext, dlen = r
    f.seek(ext * SECTOR)
    remaining = dlen
    with open(outpath, "wb") as o:
        while remaining > 0:
            chunk = f.read(min(SECTOR*64, remaining))
            if not chunk: break
            o.write(chunk); remaining -= len(chunk)
    print(f"extracted {target} -> {outpath} ({dlen} bytes)")

os.makedirs("/tmp/isoout", exist_ok=True)
extract("boot/vmlinuz-lts", "/tmp/isoout/vmlinuz-lts")
extract("boot/initramfs-lts", "/tmp/isoout/initramfs-lts")
# small text files for reference
extract("boot/syslinux/syslinux.cfg", "/tmp/isoout/syslinux.cfg")
extract(".alpine_release", "/tmp/isoout/alpine_release")

steps.reasoning_content:
openssh-server 9.5p1 is in the ISO apks. The extended live environment likely has openssh installed already (the extended ISO includes it in the default package set). If not, I can `apk add openssh` from the local apks (the ISO is a local repo, and the live boot sets up the apks repo pointing at the cdrom).

Let me mark task 1 complete and move to booting. I'll write an expect script that boots and configures.

Let me think about the expect script carefully. Key steps:

1. spawn qemu (in background-ish, but expect controls it)
2. Wait for login prompt. Send "root\n".
3. Wait for shell "# " prompt.
4. Run a heredoc/sequence of commands to:
   a. Set root password: `echo 'root:password123' | chpasswd`
   b. Ensure sshd config allows root password login. The default sshd_config has `#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password` (commented → default is "prohibit-password" in OpenSSH 9.5? Actually default PermitRootLogin is "prohibit-password" which means root can't login with password). I need to set `PermitRootLogin yes`. Also ensure PasswordAuthentication yes (default yes).
   c. Generate/ensure config: 
      `sed -i 's/^#\?PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config`
      `sed -i 's/^#\?PasswordAuthentication.*/PasswordAuthentication yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config`
   d. Ensure sshd is installed; if not, `apk add openssh`.
   e. Start sshd: `rc-service sshd start` (generates host keys on first start). Or `/usr/sbin/sshd` directly. Using rc-service is cleaner for openrc. Actually, `rc-service sshd start` runs the init script which generates host keys if missing.
   f. Verify sshd is listening on 22: `rc-status` or `netstat -tnlp | grep 22`.

The challenge: doing this reliably over expect with a slow TCG boot. Let me write robust expect.

Approach for reliability: After login, I'll send a marker-based command execution so I can detect completion. E.g., run a script that ends each section with a unique echo marker, and expect waits for the marker. This avoids prompt-matching ambiguity.

Actually, a cleaner and very robust approach: write the configuration as a single shell script, then have the guest execute it. But I can't easily copy a file into the guest without ssh (chicken-and-egg). However, I can type the script via expect (heredoc) or type commands one per line with markers.

Better idea: Use expect to send a sequence of commands, each followed by `echo DONE_<n>`, and wait for DONE_<n>. This gives reliable synchronization.

Even better: pipe a script into sh via a single line. But multiline typing in expect is fine.

Let me think about the password issue with expect + ssh for verification. I don't have sshpass. But I can verify ssh using expect too (spawn ssh, expect password prompt, send password, expect prompt, run a command). That's a clean verification without sshpass.

Actually, I realize there might be an even simpler approach for the whole thing. Instead of live-boot + manual config each time, I could just do the live boot once, configure, and that's it — the user only needs ssh working now. The VM stays running in the background. So I don't need persistence. 

Let me structure:
1. Boot QEMU in background (detached), serial → a unix socket or pty.
2. Use expect (or a python pexpect-style script) to talk to the serial socket, configure sshd.
3. Verify with ssh via expect.

I have `expect` available. Let me use expect for driving serial. But running QEMU detached with serial on a unix socket is cleaner than expect spawning qemu (which ties qemu's lifetime to expect). Let me do:

- Start QEMU in background with `-serial unix:/tmp/serial.sock,server,nowait` and `-monitor unix:/tmp/monitor.sock,server,nowait` and `-daemonize`? `-daemonize` requires serial/monitor to be redirected (not stdio) — yes that works. With -daemonize, qemu forks to background. 

Wait, can I use `-daemonize` with `-display none`? Yes. And `-serial unix:...,server,nowait` + `-monitor unix:...,server,nowait`. Then connect to the sockets with a small python script (socket) or `socat` (not available) or `nc -U`. I have `nc` — does it support -U (unix socket)? OpenBSD nc supports -U. Let me check. Or I use python to connect to the unix socket and drive it.

Actually, the cleanest: use expect to spawn `nc -U /tmp/serial.sock` or a python unix-socket client. But expect is really designed for spawning a process and talking to its stdio. 

Alternative clean approach: spawn QEMU directly under expect with serial on stdio (`-nographic` or `-serial stdio -display none -monitor none`), do the configuration, and at the end of the expect script, detach so qemu keeps running. But if expect exits, qemu (child) might get killed. With `-daemonize` we avoid that, but then expect can't use stdio.

Let me reconsider. The robust pattern:

Use python with pexpect? Not installed probably. Let me use a python script using the `pexpect`? Check. Probably not available. I'll use raw expect.

Plan: 
- Use expect to spawn qemu directly with `-nographic`. The expect process talks to qemu's serial via stdio. 
- After configuration is done and ssh verified, I keep expect/qemu running? No — expect script will end, killing qemu.

Hmm, the requirement is that the VM stays up so the user can ssh. So I need qemu to persist after my configuration session ends.

Solution: Two-phase.
Phase 1: Start qemu daemonized (serial + monitor on unix sockets). qemu runs independently in background.
Phase 2: Connect to serial socket via expect (spawning a socket client) to configure. When expect exits, qemu keeps running (it's daemonized).
Phase 3: Verify ssh (expect-spawned ssh or direct).

For connecting to unix socket from expect, I need a stdio-to-unix-socket bridge. `nc -U` might work. Let me check nc capabilities. Or I write a tiny python bridge: `python3 -c "..."` that connects to the unix socket and pumps stdin/stdout. Actually simplest: write a small python script `unixcat.py` that connects socket→stdio bidirectionally, and expect spawns that.

Actually, python can do the whole interaction without expect: open the unix socket, read until prompt, send commands, read markers. I can write a python "console driver" that:
- connects to /tmp/serial.sock
- reads in a loop
- sends commands
- matches expected output

This avoids expect entirely and is more controllable. Let me do that — a python driver script for the serial console.

But timing/reading is the tricky part. I'll implement a `read_until(pattern, timeout)` that reads from socket until pattern appears or timeout. Then `send(line)`.

Let me structure the python driver:
1. connect to serial unix socket
2. read_until("login:", timeout=180) — boot may take a while under TCG
3. send "root\n"
4. read_until a shell prompt. I'll detect by sending a marker: after login, send "echo READY_$$.\n"? Can't, not logged in yet. Instead read_until a prompt regex like "# " or "localhost:~#". The Alpine root prompt is typically "localhost:~#" or just "# ". Let me read_until "#" with timeout.
   - To be safe, after seeing "#", send `echo SHTART\n` and read_until "SHTART" to confirm we're at a shell. Actually login as root with empty password: getty prompts "Password:" too (even if empty). With empty password, I send empty line. Let me handle: after "login:", send "root\n", then expect either "Password:" or "#". If "Password:", send "\n" (empty).

Hmm, empty password login: when root has no password, some getty/login configs still ask for password and accept empty. Alpine's login: if password field is empty/!, login may allow no password prompt or accept empty. Typically Alpine live ISO root has empty password and `login` asks "Password:" and pressing enter logs in. Let me handle both: after sending "root\n", if I see "Password:", send "\n".

Let me write the driver to be robust with a sequence of commands and markers.

Configuration commands (after shell confirmed):
```
# marker to sync
PS1='' ; echo BOOTCONFIG_START
# install/ensure openssh (from local repo; -c = no network needed, uses cdrom)
apk add --no-cache openssh openssh-server 2>&1 | tail -2 ; echo APK_DONE_$?
# set root password
echo 'root:password123' | chpasswd ; echo PASSWD_DONE_$?
# enable root password login
sed -i 's/^#\?PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
sed -i 's/^#\?PasswordAuthentication.*/PasswordAuthentication yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
grep -q '^PermitRootLogin yes' /etc/ssh/sshd_config || echo 'PermitRootLogin yes' >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config
echo SED_DONE
# start sshd (generates host keys)
rc-service sshd start 2>&1 | tail -3 ; echo SSHD_START_DONE_$?
# confirm listening
netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep ':22 ' ; echo LISTEN_DONE
echo BOOTCONFIG_END
```

I'll wait for markers in sequence with generous timeouts.

For verification (phase 3), I'll do it from the host with python+expect-like on ssh. Or simpler: use expect to spawn ssh. Since I have expect, I'll spawn `ssh -p 2222 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null root@localhost`, expect "password:", send "password123\n", expect prompt "#", send "echo SSH_OK_$$; uname -a\n", read marker, then send "exit\n". 

Actually let me use python with pexpect? Not available. Use expect (tcl) for the ssh verification — straightforward.

Let me also reconsider memory and boot. TCG boot of Alpine lts kernel + initramfs + modloop load: the modloop is 172MB squashfs loaded into RAM. With -m 2048 that's fine. Boot under TCG could take 1-3 minutes. I'll set timeouts ~300s for boot.

Let me also make sure networking works: user-mode net with hostfwd. The guest gets DHCP from QEMU's built-in server (10.0.2.2 gateway, 10.0.2.15 guest). Alpine live boot may or may not bring up eth0 automatically. With OpenRC, the live ISO sets up eth0 via /etc/network/interfaces with dhcp? The Alpine live boot runs `setup-interfaces`? Actually the live ISO auto-configures networking? Not always. Hmm. 

Wait — does the guest even need network up for sshd to accept host-forwarded connections? QEMU user-mode hostfwd forwards host:2222 to guest:22. For this to work, sshd must listen on 0.0.0.0:22 (or the guest IP 10.0.2.15:22) AND the guest's network interface must be up so the TCP stack responds. Actually, hostfwd works by QEMU's SLIRP connecting to the guest IP on port 22. If the guest interface (eth0) has the 10.0.2.15 IP and is up, SLIRP forwards there. If eth0 is down (no IP), the connection to 10.0.2.15:22 will fail (no route / interface down). So I DO need eth0 up with DHCP.

On Alpine live boot, networking: The live ISO includes a boot service that may bring up the network. Actually, I recall Alpine's live ISO runs `setup-interfaces -a -m` ? Not exactly. Let me just configure it manually in the driver: `ifup eth0` or set up DHCP. Safer: run `setup-interfaces` won't be non-interactive. I'll do:
```
ip link set eth0 up
udhcpc -i eth0   # busybox dhcp client
```
Or use the openrc way: `rc-service networking start` after ensuring /etc/network/interfaces has eth0 dhcp. Let me just do udhcpc directly which is simplest and reliable:
```
ip link set eth0 up
udhcpc -i eth0 -q -t 5 2>&1 | tail -2 ; echo DHCP_DONE_$?
ip addr show eth0
```

But wait — what's the interface name? With virtio-net-pci, it's eth0 (Alpine doesn't use predictable naming by default, so eth0). Good. Actually, modern Alpine with the lts kernel — interface naming is still eth0 (no systemd/udev predictable naming). Good.

So I'll add DHCP bring-up before starting sshd (or after; sshd listens regardless but needs eth0 up for connections).

Let me also double check: does Alpine live auto-start networking? If it does, my udhcpc is redundant but harmless (might get a second DHCP). I'll just ensure eth0 is up.

Let me now also reconsider: maybe simpler to skip virtio and use `-device e1000` for guaranteed driver. Alpine lts has virtio-net though. virtio-net is fine and faster. I'll use virtio-net-pci. If it fails I'll switch. Let me keep virtio.

Actually, to minimize risk on driver/module loading (the initramfs loads virtio modules from modloop), virtio-net should be present in Alpine lts modloop. Fine.

Now, about host key generation and first sshd start: `rc-service sshd start` runs /etc/init.d/sshd which calls ssh-keygen to create host keys if missing, then starts sshd. Good.

One more: PermitRootLogin default in OpenSSH 9.5 is "prohibit-password". My sed sets it to "yes". PasswordAuthentication default is "yes" but I set it explicitly. Good. Also need to make sure there's no `UsePAM` issue — Alpine openssh doesn't use PAM by default (UsePAM no), auth via /etc/shadow directly. chpasswd updates shadow. Good.

Let me write everything now.

First, the QEMU launch (daemonized, sockets). Let me write a launcher script.

QEMU command:
```
qemu-system-x86_64 \
  -name alpine \
  -accel tcg,thread=multi \
  -m 2048 \
  -smp 2 \
  -kernel /tmp/isoout/vmlinuz-lts \
  -initrd /tmp/isoout/initramfs-lts \
  -append "modules=loop,squashfs,sd-mod,usb-storage console=ttyS0,115200" \
  -cdrom /app/alpine.iso \
  -drive file=/app/alpine-disk.qcow2,if=virtio,format=qcow2 \
  -netdev user,id=net0,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22 \
  -device virtio-net-pci,netdev=net0 \
  -display none \
  -serial unix:/tmp/serial.sock,server,nowait \
  -monitor unix:/tmp/monitor.sock,server,nowait \
  -pidfile /tmp/qemu.pid \
  -daemonize
```

Wait, `-daemonize` with `unix:...,server,nowait`: the server socket is created and QEMU waits for connections but `nowait` means it doesn't wait for a connection at startup. Good. With -daemonize, QEMU detaches. 

Hmm, but `-serial unix:...,server,nowait` — when acting as server, QEMU creates the socket and accepts ONE connection. If the client disconnects, does QEMU keep the serial socket? With `server`, QEMU listens and accepts connections; if the client drops, it goes back to listening (I think with server,nowait it re-accepts). Actually behavior: `server` makes QEMU listen; on client disconnect, with `server` it will accept a new connection. Good — my driver can connect, do work, disconnect, and qemu keeps running. 

Let me verify qemu supports `unix:...,server` syntax in 5.2. Yes, `-serial unix:/path,server[,wait]`. Good.

Let me also add `-no-reboot` so if something panics it doesn't loop. Not necessary.

Memory: 2048 should be plenty. Let me use 2048.

Actually, wait: TCG with `thread=multi` for accel — syntax `-accel tcg,thread=multi`. This enables multi-threaded TCG which speeds up SMP guests. Good for smp 2.

Let me reconsider `-smp 2` with TCG multi — fine.

Now potential issue: The Alpine live initramfs needs to find the boot media. It scans for a device with the modloop or the ISO label. With `-cdrom` it's attached as an IDE/SATA cdrom (ata). The initramfs `modules=loop,squashfs,sd-mod,usb-storage` — note it loads sd-mod (SCSI/SATA disk) and usb-storage but maybe not ata/pata for the cdrom? The `-cdrom` default on `pc` machine is IDE (ata). Hmm. Alpine's boot media scan: the initramfs uses the `nvme`, `sd_mod`, `usb-storage`, and also libata/ata_piix for IDE/SATA cdrom. The modules= line only lists loop,squashfs,sd-mod,usb-storage. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Drive the Alpine guest over the QEMU serial unix socket: login + configure sshd."""
import socket, time, re, sys

SOCK = "/tmp/serial.sock"
LOGF = open("/tmp/console.log", "ab")

def log(b):
    if isinstance(b, str): b = b.encode()
    LOGF.write(b); LOGF.flush()

s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.connect(SOCK)
s.settimeout(2.0)
print("connected to serial")

def read_until(pat, timeout):
    """Read until regex `pat` (bytes) appears in buffer; return matched text. Raise on timeout."""
    rx = re.compile(pat)
    buf = b""
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            data = s.recv(4096)
            if data:
                buf += data
                log(data)
                m = rx.search(buf)
                if m:
                    return buf.decode("latin1", "replace")
        except socket.timeout:
            continue
    raise TimeoutError(f"timeout waiting for {pat!r}; tail=\n" + buf[-800:].decode("latin1","replace"))

def send(line):
    b = (line + "\n").encode()
    s.sendall(b)
    log(b">>> " + b)

# 1) nudge + login prompt
send("")
try:
    read_until(rb"login: ?$|login:\s", 20)
except TimeoutError:
    send("")  # maybe already past; try again
    read_until(rb"login:", 30)
send("root")
# 2) either Password: or a shell prompt
got = read_until(rb"Password:|#", 40)
if "Password:" in got:
    send("")  # empty password
    read_until(rb"#", 40)

# 3) confirm shell, disable input echo for clean marker matching
read_until(rb"#", 20)
send("stty -echo")
send("echo ECHOOFF")
read_until(rb"ECHOOFF", 20)
print("shell ready, echo off")

def run(cmd, marker, timeout=90):
    send(cmd)
    out = read_until(marker.encode() if isinstance(marker,str) else marker, timeout)
    return out

# 4) is sshd already installed?
out = run("command -v sshd >/dev/null && echo SSHD_YES || echo SSHD_NO", rb"SSHD_(YES|NO)", 30)
present = "SSHD_YES" in out
print("sshd present:", present)

if not present:
    out = run("apk add --no-network openssh openssh-server openssh-keygen 2>&1 | tail -4; echo APKDONE", "APKDONE", 150)
    print("apk install done")

# 5) set root password
run("echo 'root:password123' | chpasswd; echo PASSDONE", "PASSDONE", 30)
print("password set")

# 6) sshd_config: allow root password login
run(
    "sed -i 's/^#\\?PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config;"
    "sed -i 's/^#\\?PasswordAuthentication.*/PasswordAuthentication yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config;"
    "grep -q '^PermitRootLogin yes' /etc/ssh/sshd_config || echo 'PermitRootLogin yes' >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config;"
    "grep -q '^PasswordAuthentication yes' /etc/ssh/sshd_config || echo 'PasswordAuthentication yes' >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config;"
    "echo CFGDONE", "CFGDONE", 30)
print("sshd_config done")

# 7) bring up networking (eth0) so host-forwarded connections reach sshd
run("ip link set eth0 up; udhcpc -i eth0 -t 10 -n 2>&1 | tail -3; echo NETDONE", "NETDONE", 60)
run("ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep inet; echo IPDONE", "IPDONE", 20)
print("network up")

# 8) start sshd (init script generates host keys on first start)
out = run("rc-service sshd restart 2>&1 | tail -5; echo STARTDONE", "STARTDONE", 90)
print("sshd start output:", out[-300:])

# 9) confirm it is listening on :22
out = run("(netstat -tln 2>/dev/null || ss -tln 2>/dev/null) | grep ':22 ' ; echo LISTENDONE", "LISTENDONE", 30)
listening = ":22" in out and ("0.0.0.0" in out or "*" in out or "10.0.2" in out or "127.0.0.1" in out)
print("LISTEN:", listening)
print(out)

print("=== CONFIG COMPLETE ===")
s.close()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Drive Alpine guest over serial: ensure root shell, then configure sshd."""
import socket, time, re

SOCK = "/tmp/serial.sock"
LOGF = open("/tmp/console.log", "ab")
def log(b):
    if isinstance(b, str): b = b.encode()
    LOGF.write(b); LOGF.flush()

s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.connect(SOCK)
s.settimeout(2.0)
print("connected")

def read_until(pat, timeout):
    rx = re.compile(pat); buf = b""; deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            data = s.recv(4096)
            if data:
                buf += data; log(data)
                m = rx.search(buf)
                if m: return buf.decode("latin1","replace")
        except socket.timeout: continue
    raise TimeoutError(f"timeout {pat!r}; tail=\n"+buf[-600:].decode("latin1","replace"))

def send(line):
    b=(line+"\n").encode(); s.sendall(b); log(b">>> "+b)

# --- get to a known root-shell state ---
send("\x03")          # Ctrl-C to clear any partial line
time.sleep(1)
send("")              # newline -> fresh prompt
got = read_until(rb"(login:|localhost:~#|alpine:~#|#\s)", 25)
print("initial detect:", repr(got[-120:]))

if "login:" in got:
    send("root")
    g2 = read_until(rb"(Password:|#)", 40)
    if "Password:" in g2:
        send("")
        read_until(rb"#", 40)
# Now ensure we have a prompt
send("\x03"); send("echo SH_ATTACHED")
read_until(rb"SH_ATTACHED", 25)
print("at root shell")

# disable echo for clean marker matching
send("stty -echo; echo ECHOOFF")
read_until(rb"ECHOOFF", 20)

def run(cmd, marker, timeout=120):
    send(cmd)
    return read_until(marker.encode() if isinstance(marker,str) else marker, timeout)

# openssh present?
out = run("command -v sshd >/dev/null && echo SSHD_YES || echo SSHD_NO", rb"SSHD_(YES|NO)", 30)
present = "SSHD_YES" in out
print("sshd binary present:", present)
if not present:
    run("apk add --no-network openssh openssh-server openssh-keygen 2>&1 | tail -4; echo APKDONE", "APKDONE", 180)
    print("openssh installed")

# root password
run("echo 'root:password123' | chpasswd; echo PASSDONE", "PASSDONE", 30)
print("root password set to password123")

# sshd_config
run(
 "sed -i 's/^#\\?PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config;"
 "sed -i 's/^#\\?PasswordAuthentication.*/PasswordAuthentication yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config;"
 "grep -q '^PermitRootLogin yes' /etc/ssh/sshd_config || echo 'PermitRootLogin yes' >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config;"
 "grep -q '^PasswordAuthentication yes' /etc/ssh/sshd_config || echo 'PasswordAuthentication yes' >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config;"
 "echo CFGDONE", "CFGDONE", 30)
print("sshd_config updated")

# networking
run("ip link set eth0 up; udhcpc -i eth0 -t 10 -n 2>&1 | tail -3; echo NETDONE", "NETDONE", 60)
out = run("ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep inet; echo IPDONE", "IPDONE", 20)
print("eth0:", out.strip().splitlines()[-2] if len(out.splitlines())>1 else out[-120:])

# start sshd
out = run("rc-service sshd restart 2>&1 | tail -6; echo STARTDONE", "STARTDONE", 120)
print("sshd start:", out[-260:].replace("\n"," | "))

# verify listening
out = run("(netstat -tln 2>/dev/null || ss -tln 2>/dev/null) | grep ':22' ; echo LISTENDONE", "LISTENDONE", 30)
print("=== listen check ===")
print(out)
print("=== CONFIG COMPLETE ===")
s.close()

import socket, time, re
SOCK="/tmp/serial.sock"

def read_until(pat,timeout):

    while time.time()<deadline:
